body:
From design-agent, 03-operate design (packet qitem-20261003082416-b1057e7a): two territory grants
needed for the functional suite, both test-side, both small. Recommended default: grant both.

1. src/functionalTest/resources/application-functional.properties (one comment + two lines).
   The rate limiter sits on every request in every functional context. Slices 01 and 02 send far
   more than 60 creates per minute from MockMvc's default 127.0.0.1 (01's create, idempotency and
   observability journeys alone), so with the shipped defaults the existing suite would start
   answering 429. The overlay raises both budgets for the suite
   (urlshort.rate-limit.create-per-minute / redirect-per-minute); 03's own limiter journeys set
   the shipped 60/600 back explicitly in their @SpringBootTest properties (inline test properties
   outrank the profile file). This is the documented place for suite-wide settings (ADR-0004).
   Alternative without a grant: a systemProperty on the functionalTest task in build.gradle.kts
   (03's territory); rejected as less discoverable than the overlay the suite already uses.

2. src/functionalTest/java/dev/urlshort/link/FunctionalClock.java (add freeze(); reset() also
   unfreezes). The SPEC's limiter ACs run on "a frozen suite-controlled clock" (AC-1 to AC-10,
   AC-3(a) needs exact 999 ms / 1 ms steps). FunctionalClock is the one application Clock the
   whole suite shares (offset-based today, real time keeps running). A frozen mode is about six
   lines and changes nothing for existing callers. Alternative: a second, limiter-only time source
   bean; rejected because it splits "the service clock" in two and every limiter instant would no
   longer be the Clock bean's (ADR-0005).

02-analytics is unaffected: it uses FunctionalClock read-only and merges first; 03 rebases.
summary: 03-operate design: two test-side territory grants (application-functional.properties budgets; FunctionalClock freeze)
